items.title: Students’ academic freedom central to Africa’s democratic future – Prof Appiagyei-Atua
items.description: Professor of International Law and Human Rights at the University of Ghana School of Law, Prof Kwadwo Appiagyei-Atua, has emphasised the importance of students’ academic freedom in strengthening democratic practices and shaping the future of democracy in Africa. He made the observation while delivering the University of Ghana’s ninth Inaugural Lecture for the 2025/2026 academic year at the Great Hall. The lecture, titled “The Student Question: Reclaiming Academic Freedom for Democratic Renewal in Africa,” was the final Inaugural Lecture in the University’s series for the academic year. Prof Appiagyei-Atua examined academic freedom within the wider context of Africa’s intellectual heritage, colonialism, university governance, student participation and democratic development. He challenged the conventional view that the State is the main threat to academic freedom, arguing that greater attention must also be paid to the structures and relationships within universities themselves. According to him, academic freedom can be undermined by several actors, including university management, academics and students. He noted that internal structures and power relations within universities could limit students’ ability to participate meaningfully in institutional governance and academic decision-making, despite their status as members and key stakeholders of the academic community. A major focus of the lecture was the position of students within the academic freedom framework. Drawing on the 1990 Dar es Salaam Declaration, Prof Appiagyei-Atua highlighted students’ rights to freedom of study, freedom to dissent, participation in academic programmes and involvement in university governance. He stressed that students are rights-holders because they are members of academic communities and should therefore have a meaningful voice in decisions affecting their education and the institutions they attend. Prof Appiagyei-Atua also examined the marginalisation of students within university structures. He described academic communities as vertically structured institutions in which students often occupy a subordinate position, despite being among their primary stakeholders. He argued that academic freedom could exist in a formal sense while students’ substantive freedom remained restricted by unequal power relations and institutional structures. The lecture also examined student politics and the influence of partisan politics on university campuses. Prof Appiagyei-Atua observed that the involvement of political parties in student leadership could weaken independent student activism, fuel distrust, and undermine confidence in student representation. To address these concerns, he proposed measures to strengthen independent student leadership and representation. These include transparent campaigns, non-partisan student leadership and stronger collaboration between student bodies and civil society organisations. Prof Appiagyei-Atua also called for the democratisation of the classroom, teaching methods and university governance. He argued that universities should move away from traditional approaches in which students are primarily treated as recipients of knowledge. Instead, he advocated approaches that promote dialogue, critical thinking and the co-creation of knowledge between students and academics. As part of his proposals, he presented a collaborative governance model involving the State, universities, faculty, students and civil society. The model is based on distributed authority, horizontal consultation, mutual accountability and recognition of the distinct but interconnected roles of the various stakeholders. Prof Appiagyei-Atua linked the experience of students on university campuses to the wider development of democracy in African societies. He argued that universities provide important spaces for developing democratic habits and that students’ experiences of participation, representation and accountability can influence how they engage with democratic institutions after leaving university. He therefore called for students’ academic freedom to be understood as more than an issue limited to university campuses. In his view, protecting students’ rights to participate, dissent and contribute to decision-making can help strengthen democratic values across society. Chairperson for the occasion and Vice-Chancellor of the University of Ghana, Prof Nana Aba Appiah Amfo, praised the lecture, describing it as intriguing and thought-provoking. She commended Prof Appiagyei-Atua for the perspectives he presented on students’ academic freedom and its relationship with democratic development. Prof Appiah Amfo acknowledged the challenges surrounding academic freedom and student participation within universities, while stressing the need to create an environment in which all members of university communities can contribute meaningfully to institutional life. On behalf of the University community, she also congratulated Prof Appiagyei-Atua on his progression through the academic ranks to become a full professor. She recognised his contributions to international law, human rights scholarship and academic discourse. In earlier remarks, the Registrar of the University of Ghana, Mr Michael Opare Atuah, said Inaugural Lectures remain an important University tradition through which the institution recognises and celebrates the scholarly contributions of its academics. He congratulated Prof Appiagyei-Atua on delivering his Inaugural Lecture and noted that it was the final lecture in the University’s series for the 2025/2026 academic year. He also congratulated the other professors who delivered their Inaugural Lectures during the academic year. Following the lecture, Prof Appiagyei-Atua received presentations from the School of Law, the Research and Innovation Directorate, Legon Hall, and his family, among others. He also received a package from Promasidor Ghana, which sponsors the University of Ghana’s Inaugural Lectures.

items.description: Sept 12 (Reuters) - An understanding between Iran and Oman does not provide for the immediate reopening of the Strait of Hormuz but establishes the basis on which it could reopen, an Iranian source told the semi-official Tasnim news agency on Saturday. The source said the arrangement would be a step towards Iran exercising sovereignty over the strait and that its reopening depended entirely on the United States meeting Tehran's conditions. items.title: Mahama announces maize processing plant for Sissala area to tackle glut
items.description: President John Dramani Mahama has announced plans to establish a maize processing plant in the Sissala area of the Upper West Region as part of efforts to tackle the recurring glut faced by maize farmers. The facility, he said, will create a reliable market for maize producers while adding value to the crop for both domestic consumption and export. President Mahama said the initiative was intended to encourage increased production by ensuring farmers have a market for their harvest. “We are going to set up a maize processing plant in the Sissala area. The plant will not only buy the maize, but it will also process the maize for the market and for export, and so I believe that this glut will become a thing of the past,” he said during a citizens’ engagement at the University of Business and Integrated Development Studies on Saturday, September 12. President Mahama also announced plans to increase funding to the National Food Buffer Stock Company to enable it to purchase more surplus maize. He said inadequate storage capacity had constrained the company’s ability to absorb excess production and disclosed that silos would be constructed at its storage centres to expand its capacity. “Aside from that, we are increasing the amount of money that we are giving to Buffer Stock to off-take the excess maize,” he added.

items.title: Attaque de drones contre l’Arabie saoudite : l’Algérie réagit
items.description: L’Algérie a réagi ce samedi aux attaques de drones lancées depuis l’Irak contre l’Arabie saoudite . « L'Algérie condamne fermement l'attaque au cours de laquelle des drones ont ciblé le Royaume frère d'Arabie saoudite, en frappant l'oléoduc Est-Ouest dans les régions de Riyad et de Médine », a indiqué le ministère des Affaires étrangères dans un communiqué. Pour l’Algérie, cette « attaque odieuse » est une « violation flagrante de la souveraineté du Royaume, une menace pour sa sécurité et sa stabilité, et une atteinte à ses ressources et à son infrastructure économique », a ajouté le communiqué. L’Algérie réaffirme sa solidarité avec l’Arabie saoudite « Tout en réaffirmant sa pleine solidarité avec le Royaume frère d'Arabie saoudite face à cette agression », l'Algérie apporte son soutien à Riyad pour « toutes les mesures prises pour protéger sa sécurité, sa stabilité et son intégrité territoriale ». Lancés à partir de l’Irak, des drones ont visé l’oléoduc Est-Ouest qui transporte 7 millions de barils par jour. L’Arabie saoudite a annoncé vendredi la fermeture de ce pipeline qui est utilisé pour contourner le verrouillage du détroit d’Ormuz par l’Iran. Le ministère des Affaires étrangères saoudien a fait état de blessés et de dégâts matériels après cette attaque qui a visé un oléoduc stratégique qui permet à l’Arabie saoudite d’atténuer les effets des tensions au niveau du détroit d’Ormuz sur ses exportations de brut. Ce pipeline relie le champ pétrolifère d'Abqaiq près du golfe Persique au port de Yanbu (Médine) sur la mer Rouge. L’article Attaque de drones contre l’Arabie saoudite : l’Algérie réagit est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: UNN sued over Peter Obi’s academic records
items.description: A Labour Party (LP) chieftain, Abayomi Arabambi, has sued the University of Nigeria Nsukka (UNN) over the alleged refusal to release details of the academic record of Peter Obi, the presidential candidate of the Nigerian Democratic Congress (NDC). Arabambi, in a fresh suit, said he had requested a certified true copy (CTC) of Obi’s certificate number D000198 in respect of a Bachelor of Arts in Philosophy issued in 1984 in line with the Freedom of Information Act, but the institution turned down his demand. In the originating motion marked FHC/ABJ/CS/2144/2026 and filed by his lawyer, Anderson Asemota, on Sept. 9 at the Federal High Court in Abuja, said letters had been written to the university. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that in the court documents made available on Saturday, the applicant, a former factional spokesperson for LP, named the VC and UNN as 1st and 2nd respondents. He is, therefore, seeking an order of mandamus compelling the respondents to perform their statutory duty under the FoI Act, 2011, by determining and responding to his request dated July 16 in accordance with the provisions of the Act. According to Arabambi in the affidavit setting out the facts, by a letter dated 16th July, 2026, the applicant requested a CTC of Certificate No. D000198, stated to have been issued by the University of Nigeria, Nsukka, to Gregory Peter Onwubuasi Obi in respect of a Bachelor of Arts Degree in Philosophy in 1984. “The applicant also requested a Certified True Copy of the certificate, academic record or other official records upon which the said degree was predicated. “The said request was duly delivered to and received by the respondents on 6th August, 2026. “The applicant expressly made the request pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, 2011, and stated the public-interest and accountability basis for the request. “The respondents failed and/or neglected to provide the requested information within the period prescribed by the Act,” he said. Arabambi stated that the respondents did not communicate to him a written notice of refusal identifying the specific provision of the Act relied upon for refusing access. “The applicant consequently sent a reminder letter dated 31st August, 2026, reiterating the original request and again demanding the requested records. “The reminder letter was delivered to and received by the respondents on 1st September, 2026, as evidenced by the delivery receipt,” he said. Arabambi, in the affidavit deposed to by Chuku Maudlyn, a litigation secretary in the law firm of Messrs Neplus Ultra Attorneys, averred that the delivery receipt identified the receiver as the VC and the destination as the UNN. “As at the commencement of this action, the respondents have neither supplied the requested records nor issued a lawful written notice of refusal,” he said. The applicant, therefore, sought 19 reliefs. He prayed the court for a declaration that his written request made pursuant to the FoI Act, 2011, “constitutes a valid request for information within the contemplation of the Freedom of Information Act.” He sought an order of mandamus compelling the respondents to furnish him with a CTC of certificate number D000198 issued by the university if the said certificate exists in the custody, possession or control of the respondents. Arabambi also sought an order of mandamus compelling them to furnish him with the CTC of the existing official academic and institutional records relating to the said degree and the certificate, including where they exist and are within the custody or control of the respondents. He listed the documents he sought as relevant academic records, relevant graduation/degree-award records, relevant certificate-register entries, relevant Senate or academic approval award records, and any other existing official records upon which the said degree and/or certificate was based, among other reliefs. Giving grounds for his application, Arabambi submitted that as an applicant, he has a statutory right of access to information in the custody of a public institution. According to him, the respondents are subject to the Freedom of Information Act. He said the requested information concerns a certificate expressly represented to have been issued by the UNN. He says the respondents are consequently the institution whose official records are directly relevant to his request. Arabambi said Section 4 of the Act imposes a statutory duty to respond within the prescribed period, and that they had failed to comply with that duty. “The respondents did not communicate a lawful refusal identifying any applicable exemption. “The failure therefore constitutes a refusal and/or deemed refusal under the Act,” he concluded. NAN reports that at the centre of the applicant’s complaint is what he described as multiple variations of Obi’s name across documents submitted to the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) and educational authorities. The case is yet to be assigned to a judge. (NAN) The post UNN sued over Peter Obi’s academic records appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Élections 2026 : Ilham Belfhili promet un SMIG à 6.000 DH et des aides pour les jeunes
items.description: À l’approche des élections législatives de 2026, la secrétaire générale de l’Union marocaine pour la démocratie, Ilham Belfhili, dévoile plusieurs engagements de son parti, allant de la revalorisation du SMIG à 6.000 dirhams à la gratuité des médicaments pour les personnes démunies. Le parti de l’Union marocaine pour la démocratie mise largement sur la jeunesse pour les prochaines échéances électorales. Sa secrétaire générale, Ilham Belfhili, a indiqué que 90 % des têtes de listes de sa formation sont des jeunes âgés de 23 à 35 ans. Selon elle, le parti a réussi à couvrir 55 circonscriptions locales et 10 circonscriptions régionales, soit un taux de couverture de 63,5 %, contre 14 % lors des élections de 2021. Invitée de l’émission « La route vers les élections 2026 », Belfhili a expliqué que ce choix répond à la volonté de renouveler les élites politiques et de mieux intégrer les jeunes dans la vie publique. Elle a également souligné la présence, parmi les candidatures, d’une femme en situation de handicap à la tête d’une liste régionale dans la région de Souss-Massa, ainsi que de trois candidates issues de la diaspora, résidant en France, en Espagne et en Italie. Un SMIG porté à 6.000 dirhams Sur le volet économique et social, l’Union marocaine pour la démocratie avance plusieurs propositions. Ilham Belfhili a notamment évoqué la possibilité de porter le SMIG à 6.000 dirhams, sous réserve, selon elle, de lutter efficacement contre les sources de corruption. Le parti propose également une hausse de 1.500 dirhams des salaires et une augmentation de 1.000 dirhams pour les retraités. Pour les jeunes sans emploi, une allocation mensuelle de 200 dirhams serait accordée, accompagnée de formations destinées à renforcer leurs compétences jusqu’à leur insertion professionnelle. Une autre aide de 1.500 dirhams serait destinée aux jeunes engagés dans un parcours de formation. Gratuité des soins pour les plus démunis Dans le domaine de la santé, Belfhili propose notamment de supprimer l’actuel système d’indexation évoqué par le parti et de garantir un accès gratuit aux soins à toute personne titulaire de la carte nationale d’identité. La formation souhaite également créer ce qu’elle appelle des « pharmacies de santé », permettant aux personnes démunies d’accéder gratuitement aux médicaments, tandis que les bénéficiaires de la couverture médicale ne paieraient que la différence restant à leur charge. Sur le logement, le parti propose que l’État prenne en charge la moitié du coût d’un logement pour les personnes souhaitant se marier. Le reste pourrait être financé grâce à des facilités préférentielles à un taux de 2 %. Le même dispositif serait proposé aux personnes en situation de handicap. Le programme comprend aussi une réforme de la compensation, un plafonnement des prix, l’instauration d’un impôt sur la fortune et, parallèlement, une réduction de la fiscalité sur les salaires. La lutte contre la corruption au cœur du programme La lutte contre la corruption constitue également l’un des principaux engagements avancés par Belfhili. La responsable politique affirme vouloir rompre avec la logique de « l’impunité » et avec la politique résumée par l’expression « Afwa Allah 3amma Salaf ». Elle a par ailleurs annoncé son intention de demander des comptes sur les montants consacrés au soutien du pouvoir d’achat, faisant référence aux 280 milliards de dirhams évoqués par Fouzi Lekjaa. Ilham Belfhili a également insisté sur l’importance de la participation aux prochaines élections. Elle dit notamment faire confiance aux garanties annoncées par le Roi concernant la transparence et l’intégrité du scrutin. Elle s’est dite convaincue que les structures chargées du suivi des élections réagiront fermement à toute tentative d’achat de voix, de propagande illégale ou d’atteinte à l’intégrité du processus électoral. La secrétaire générale de l’Union marocaine pour la démocratie estime enfin que les prochaines années seront déterminantes pour le Maroc, notamment concernant les grands dossiers nationaux, dont celui de l’autonomie. « Al Watan Al An » : un rapprochement qui pourrait évoluer Concernant l’alliance récemment conclue avec le Parti de la Renaissance et le Parti de l’Unité et de la Démocratie, Belfhili a précisé que « Al Watan Al An » constitue pour le moment une alliance politique et non électorale. Elle explique ce choix notamment par des contraintes organisationnelles au sein de l’un des partis partenaires. L’alliance repose néanmoins sur une coopération électorale et une convergence de visions et d’orientations. Belfhili n’exclut pas que cette entente évolue vers une alliance électorale, voire vers une fusion, si la coopération venait à se consolider. Pour la dirigeante, le choix du slogan « Al Watan Al An » traduit une priorité claire : l’urgence de la réforme et la nécessité d’élections transparentes accompagnées d’une participation importante des citoyens. The post Élections 2026 : Ilham Belfhili promet un SMIG à 6.000 DH et des aides pour les jeunes appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: LDC dela CAF: le MAS qualifié au deuxième tour préliminaire
items.description: Le Maghreb de Fès (MAS) s’est qualifié pour le deuxième tour préliminaire de la Ligue des champions d’Afrique de football, à l’issue du match retour du premier tour préliminaire face au Rahimo FC du Burkina Faso, samedi à Ouagadougou. Les champions du Maroc en titre ont fait match nul (0-0) face à la formation burkinabè, après avoir largement remporté le match aller (4-1) à Fès. La première mi-temps de cette rencontre a été marquée par la domination de l’équipe burkinabè, qui s’est procuré plusieurs occasions franches sans toutefois parvenir à concrétiser. Au retour des vestiaires, les Fassis ont repris le contrôle du jeu, privilégiant la conservation du ballon tout en tentant de surprendre la défense adverse. Les deux équipes se sont, enfin, quittées dos à dos, un résultat qui permet au MAS, fort de son large avantage acquis à l’aller (4-1), de valider son billet au prochain tour de la prestigieuse compétition africaine des clubs. Au deuxième tour préliminaire, le représentant du football marocain affrontera le vainqueur de la double confrontation entre l’ASC Kara du Togo et l’ASEC Mimosas de Côte d’Ivoire. items.title: Avis de recrutement de chauffeurs coursiers (04) et d’une maitresse d’internat
items.description: AVIS DE RECRUTEMENT. Un important Complexe Scolaire moderne situé dans la commune de Saaba au Burkina Faso recrute pour emploi immédiat sous contrat CDD : Des chauffeurs coursiers (04) Une maitresse d’internat Chauffeur coursier Profil : Être titulaire du permis de conduire catégorie D et savoir s’exprimer en Français, avoir au moins une expérience pratique dans la conduite. Activités : Assurer la conduite des élèves à bord du bus scolaire, effectuer des courses au bénéfice de l’Administration, assurer l’entretien et le nettoyage régulier des véhicules du parc auto du Complexe Scolaire, tenir à jour les documents de bord des véhicules, veiller au respect de la validité des différents documents légaux du véhicule (carte grise, assurance, visite technique) veiller à la sécurité des passagers pendant le transport, assurer le suivi du fonctionnement normal des véhicules et rendre compte de toute défaillance, respecter les règles de sécurité et de limitation de vitesse établie, assurer les tâches que pourraient lui confiées sa hiérarchie. Compétences : Être dévoué et consciencieux, savoir lire et écrire, être de bonne moralité, être méthodique et organisé, avoir une maîtrise des règles élémentaires de sécurité, avoir le sens du respect de la hiérarchie, avoir des connaissances générales en mécanique, avoir un esprit d’initiative et d’anticipation, faire preuve de loyauté, de rigueur et de don de soi. Maitresse d’internat Missions : Surveillance et encadrement des élèves en internat (nuit et périodes hors cours), animation de la vie collective, veille à la sécurité et au respect du règlement intérieur. Profil recherché : Sens des responsabilités, capacité d'écoute, autorité bienveillante et expérience souhaitée dans l'encadrement de jeunes. Candidatures Les personnes intéressées devront envoyer leurs candidatures uniquement par voie électronique à l’adresse suivante : recrutementcs56@gmail.com en précisant obligatoirement en objet du mail le titre du poste, au plus tard le 19 septembre 2026 à 17h TU. Composition du dossier. Un curriculum vitae (CV) actualisé et sincère de trois pages au maximum avec les contacts de 3 personnes de référence, Une lettre de motivation de deux pages au maximum adressée au Directeur du Complexe Scolaire et faisant ressortir l’intérêt du candidat pour le poste, Une copie légalisée du diplôme requis, Les copies légalisées du/des certificats ou attestation de travail, Une copie légalisée du permis de conduire catégorie D pour le poste de chauffeur coursier. Procédure de recrutement Le recrutement va se dérouler selon les différentes étapes suivantes : Présélection sur dossier, Test et Entretien devant un jury. Notez Bien : Seul(e)s les candidat(e)s présélectionné(e)s seront contacté(e)s. items.title: El Madring alumbra al mejor Lando Norris, que firma la primera ‘pole’ de la historia del circuito
items.description: Dejen paso al campeón del mundo para que pueda lucir su corona en Madrid, donde este domingo (15:00; Dazn) liderará el pelotón cuando se apaguen los semáforos y, si no la pifia, hasta que cruce la meta, 57 vueltas después. A Lando Norris no le vio venir nadie en un Gran Premio de España que se le puso cuesta arriba por culpa de una avería en la caja de cambios de su monoplaza que le dejó metido en el garaje en el segundo entrenamiento libre. Un problemón en un circuito nuevo y tan implacable como el Madring , abrazado por muros y minado por trampas. Ocurre, sin embargo, que este tipo de trazados urbanos son el escenario ideal para que los mejores pilotos saquen sus mejores vueltas, y la que Norris se inventó en los estertores de la tercera eliminatoria de la cronometrada (Q3) fue, en sus propias palabras, la mejor de su vida. Una machada que le valió al chico de Bristol su tercera pole position de la temporada, todas ellas en las últimas cuatro paradas del calendario, una inercia que confirma el paso adelante dado por McLaren en Hungría , antes del verano, cuando revitalizó el bólido papaya con la actualización que hizo efecto de forma inmediata. La primera línea la cerrará Kimi Antonelli, que se quedó solo a 11 milésimas y que seguramente es el único que tiene a su alcance una mínima posibilidad de poner en riesgo el triunfo del británico. Carlos Sainz y Fernando Alonso se quedaron en la primera criba (Q1) y arrancarán el 17º y el 18º, respectivamente. Sin embargo, Sainz partirá finalmente desde la vigésima casilla de la parrilla después de recibir una sanción de tres posiciones por bloquear una vuelta rápida a Valtteri Bottas (Cadillac) durante la calificación. Esto ayudó a Alonso a ocupar finalmente la plaza 17ª. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Ebola en RDC: le pic de l’épidémie est passé, selon les autorités
items.description: En République démocratique du Congo (RDC), les autorités sanitaires annoncent une décrue de l’épidémie d’Ebola, quatre mois après sa déclaration. 10 des 61 zones de santé alors touchées n’avaient enregistré aucun nouveau cas, depuis au moins 21 jours, mais cette amélioration intervient au moment où le bilan franchit les 7 000 cas confirmés. items.title: Des journalistes ouest-africains en immersion au siège de QNET
items.description: Après un voyage de près de deux jours, les 9 et 10 septembre, des journalistes ouest-africains sont arrivés à Kuala Lumpur, en Malaisie, où ils ont visité, le lendemain, le siège de QNET. KUALA LUMPUR – Des journalistes de huit pays d’Afrique de l’Ouest, notamment du Bénin, du Ghana, du Liberia, du Nigeria, du Togo, de la Sierra Leone et du Sénégal, séjournent depuis le 10 septembre et jusqu’au 17 septembre à Kuala Lumpur, la capitale malaisienne. Ils sont invités par l’entreprise QNET, qui célèbre ses 28 ans d’existence, pour visiter son siège, la QI Tower, et participer à la convention mondiale qui se tiendra sur l’île de Penang, à environ 350 kilomètres de la capitale. Cette visite de représentants des médias africains a pour objectif de leur offrir un aperçu des activités de l’entreprise à l’échelle mondiale, notamment en Afrique, où elle est présente dans plusieurs pays. Elle a également permis aux journalistes d’observer, de manipuler et de tester différents produits, dont certains bénéficient, dans des pays comme le Sénégal, de certifications internationales basées sur des recherches. Il s’agit d’une gamme variée de produits et de services axés notamment sur le bien-être et la santé. Au cours de la visite guidée, les représentants de l’entreprise ont également présenté les valeurs de QNET, qui mettent en avant les questions liées à l’éducation et au social. Des activités dénoncées Lors des échanges, les responsables de QNET ont toutefois dénoncé certaines activités menées sans l’autorisation de leur structure et utilisant la marque de leurs produits. « Accueillir les médias nous permet de démontrer notre dévouement au service des populations », a déclaré la porte-parole de l’entreprise. Elle a rappelé que l’institution, qui emploie plus de 2 000 personnes à travers le monde, se considère comme une entreprise sérieuse et entend répondre aux accusations d’arnaque dont elle fait l’objet. En plus de ses produits dédiés au bien-être et à la santé des populations, l’entreprise a créé, en collaboration avec l’État de Perak, en Malaisie, une université de recherche. Celle-ci a formé des chercheurs de plusieurs générations et de différents pays. Des chercheurs, des employés et des journalistes participent d’ailleurs à la convention mondiale, qui rassemblera des centaines de personnes venues d’environ 30 pays. Cette rencontre vise notamment à favoriser le réseautage, le développement professionnel et la création de communautés. J’ai notamment corrigé « Chana » en « Ghana », « Sierra Léonne » en « Sierra Leone », « sont arrivée » en « sont arrivés », ainsi que plusieurs formulations et accords. De notre envoyé spécial en Malaisie, Eugène KALY

items.description: The family of the late National Chairman of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Alhaji Bamanga Tukur, has fixed Sunday for the burial of the elder statesman. items.title: Remembering 9/11, 25 Years Later
items.description: Editor's Note: Washington Week With The Atlantic is a partnership between NewsHour Productions, WETA, and The Atlantic airing every Friday on PBS stations nationwide. Check your local listings , watch full episodes here , or listen to the weekly podcast here . It has been 25 years since nearly 3,000 people died in a terror attack on the World Trade Center on September 11. “As far as I’m concerned, we can never talk about them enough,” Jeffrey Goldberg, the editor in chief of The Atlantic , said last night. Panelists on Washington Week With The Atlantic joined him for a discussion about the lives that were lost, and they examined the fallout from one of the most terrifying events in the nation’s history. The Atlantic staff writer Jonathan Lemire was an intern at New York Daily News on 9/11. When he learned of the attacks on the Twin Towers, his editor sent him to nearby hospitals. “The most harrowing image from that day for me was you could look in” at the beds lined up, “and they stayed empty,” he said last night. “There weren’t the survivors that people thought could be rushed and saved.” Joining Goldberg to discuss this and more: Ann Compton, a former White House correspondent for ABC News; Sally Jenkins, a staff writer at The Atlantic ; Lemire, a staff writer at The Atlantic and a co-host of Morning Joe on MS NOW; Graeme Wood, a staff writer at The Atlantic . Watch the full episode here .

items.title: How agricultural reclamation village Al-Ray bel-Rash became beset by weapons, drugs and the informal gold trade
items.description: Two armored vehicles, a police car and two small open pick-up trucks entered the Al-Ray bel-Rash village in the Edfu district in northern Aswan in the afternoon of September 5, part of a security campaign targeting the home of Abdallah al-Hugairy. An exchange of fire that would last around two and a half hours was about to begin. Hugairy has repeatedly been implicated in incidents of gunfire and forcefully stealing cars, motorcycles and tuk tuks from villagers and dahaba (people who work in informal gold mining), according to Ahmed al-Bagga, a farmer from the village. He also says Hugairy is among those accused of killing a villager about two years ago. Bagga tells Mada Masr that Hugairy fought most of Saturday’s skirmish alone, before jumping from the roof of his house to that of a neighbor, whose livestock, “his source of livelihood,” was hit and killed by a stray bullet in the fray. Bagga says two police personnel were wounded in the uproar: the assistant investigator at the Edfu district, Mohamed Zidan, and a police conscript. News circulating about the incident recorded Zidan’s injury, without mentioning the conscript or further detailing the raid. Despite all this, Hugairy managed to escape from the village, while security forces raided another house, killed its owner — whom Bagga describes as a drug dealer — and then withdrew from the area. The next day, Hugairy returned to the village, “as if nothing had happened,” Bagga says. The eruption of violence at the beginning of the month exposes the recurring pattern that has taken root in Al-Ray bel-Rash. The village sank into deprivation in the 1990s, isolated from essential resources and services. Residents describe how these conditions gave space and air to the flourishing of informal and illicit arms and drug trades. Occasional security interventions and clashes, increasing over recent years, have done little to break these trades’ entrenchment. Instead, the volatile dynamic has deepened the isolation of both the village and its residents. The village, whose name roughly translates to sprinkle irrigation, was established only around six decades ago as part of a state-sponsored agricultural reclamation project. One of its farmers, Shazly, describes it to Mada Masr as still “the most famous village growing tomatoes in the governorate” of Aswan. So how has the village become a place whose name, for those in the area, is synonymous with drugs and weapons? The beginning of the road linking the desert to the village of Al-Ray bel-Rash in northern Aswan, September 2025. Photo: Mada Masr * * * Al-Ray bel-Rash was established in 1968 as part of an agricultural reclamation project implemented by the Upper Egypt Agricultural Company in Wadi al-Radisiyah. When the company was liquidated in 1990, the lands it had reclaimed from the desert were broken up and re-apportioned to individual farmers — the company’s former employees — at reduced prices per feddan payable with a low interest rate over a 30-year period, on condition that the employees accept their redundancy from the company and be barred from applying to government jobs in the future. It’s here that the problems begin. According to an agricultural administration employee speaking to Mada Masr on condition of anonymity, when the Upper Egypt company was active, it cultivated only around 300 of the roughly 1,500 feddans that fall within the village’s official boundaries. But when the employees became land owners, they needed to make a living from farming and accumulate money to pay off the land’s cost and the interest. So, they sought to cultivate their new plots to the fullest possible extent. The village was not equipped to host all of this activity. Wadi Radisiyah begins at the villages of Tunab and Hasaya near the Nile, deepening eastward into the desert and passing through the villages of Bassaly, Zaqlouna, Raiya, reaching Al-Ray bel-Rash and Umm Salama before approaching the Nile again at the neighboring Adwa village. Al-Ray bel-Rash is more or less in the middle of this stretch, furthest from a water source at either end and surrounded by desert. To reach the village, Nile waters must first make a long journey via lifting stations and canals. The water that was sufficient for the company to cultivate roughly one-fifth of the village’s total area was no longer enough for the new owners to cultivate the entire tract. “The company handed over the lands on the basis they had an allocated water supply. In reality, farmers did not have any water allocation for a third of their land,” the employee says. Residents’ demands for an increased water share fell on deaf ears. The project was originally classified as land to be cultivated by sprinkle irrigation — giving the village its name. The employee says that while the company itself relied on flood irrigation to cultivate the lands, once the lands were redistributed, their official classification became a retort thrown back in the face of residents’ pleas. No agricultural association was established in the village to organize water distribution, and disputes began to flare up over the scarce resource, the employee says. Now, though the land needs watering every five to eight days, the irrigation cycle in the village can extend as long as 12 or 18 days, with some fields receiving no water at all. The employee estimates that by 2024 around 80 percent of the village’s lands were barren. Although Mada Masr is unable to independently verify the figure, it is consistent with farmers’ accounts of a widespread decline in cultivated areas. The situation worsened as irrigation infrastructure deteriorated. Abdou al-Nubi, who manages the water lifting station for Al-Ray bel-Rash, tells Mada Masr that the station has not been comprehensively renovated since the project’s establishment and that another station that lifts Nile water into the valley has also not been renewed since 1996. The system’s water collection basin has not been cleaned since 1986. Some of the pumps operate at about 10 percent capacity, says Nubi, while the Wadi Radisiyah canal itself needs lining and gradient adjustment to prevent water evaporation when the volume is high. The area is ill-equipped to serve residents in other ways, too. A local administrative unit employee speaking to Mada Masr says the village has no health clinic, post office or youth center. As a result, residents have to travel about 15 km to reach the Edfu General Hospital, more than half of which, he says, is along unpaved roads. The local unit employee says that the lands in the valley designated for public services were sold off in recent years, following the liquidation of Upper Egypt company’ s assets. He adds that the land allocated for the agricultural cooperative association ended up in the hands of a man that village residents describe as a drug dealer. Even the village mosque has been closed since 2021 after the building became threatened with collapse, according to the residents who set up a prayer tent at their own expense. The deprivation extends along the valley. The main village of the reclamation project, Wadi al-Radisiyah, was once classified as among the 100 poorest villages in Egypt. It has since been included in the presidential Hayah Karima initiative. While the residents of Al-Ray bel-Rash believe their village is in a worse condition in terms of services, the village is not included in the initiative, with residents attributing the exclusion to the security situation. The conditions are compounded by the absence of public transportation serving the village. Saber, a driver from Al-Ray bel-Rash, says that during the day residents are transported back and forth by two pickup trucks — which are not equipped for carrying passengers — while at other times they rely on finding a passing truck or an agricultural tractor. Once daylight fades, the problem is no longer one of finding an appropriate vehicle but rather that drivers are worried to venture along the road at all. With the decline of agriculture and a dearth of alternatives, Shazly says drug dealers began buying land in the village and setting up outlets for their business, while leaving the land uncultivated. Land prices collapsed. A drug-trading outlet has been established next to Shazly’s own land. He says his land was previously valued at around LE400,000 and has now become worth less than half that amount. Nevertheless, he has refused an offer to sell it to a customer he described as another dealer, “so I could keep my neighbors safe from harm.” Dense areas of the invasive plant, heish, grow on abandoned farmland in Al-Ray bel-Rash, says the agricultural administration employee, lending partial concealment to dealers and users. While agricultural associations can, in theory, order landowners to clear land, some employees at the associations in neighboring villages are afraid of getting into confrontations with the owners. The same fear appears in the local unit employee’s account. He says that many government workers, including Electricity Ministry employees, are reluctant to go to the village to issue violation orders where land is being used for drug outlets or informal prospecting “mills” — the sites used by informal miners to crush and process gold-bearing rock which have also spread throughout the village over the past decade. A source who was formerly in a security role at the Edfu police precinct dates the expansion of the drug and arms trade in Wadi Radisiyah, which includes Al-Ray bel-Rash, to the years following the January revolution. He cites the 2011 kidnapping of the Tounab village mayor, Fawzy Ahmed Ali Makady, following a confrontation reportedly linked to the establishment of a drug-selling outlet in his village. Makady has not been seen since. In the following years, the valley and its villages began appearing in reports of clashes with Interior Ministry forces, with Al-Ray bel-Rash appearing particularly in reports concerning drugs and weapons. Beginning in 2020, press reports started using the phrase “Al-Ray bel-Rash dens” in coverage of security campaigns targeting the village. While weapons may have entered the village alongside the illicit drug trade, their presence has lent an extra layer of violence and volatility to local disputes. A 2020 disagreement between two families over a plot of land that escalated into an exchange of fire prompted security forces to cordon off the village. Killings spread over family or business disputes, sometimes involving shootings and stabbings — even between siblings. The disputes themselves are nothing new, according to Farag, one of the village’s farmers, but the means to settle them have changed. As he puts it, “back then, we used to fight with sticks. Now, even the slightest dispute between two families involves rifles.” More recently, the spread of informal mining has become increasingly intertwined with the other trades. In the years following the 2011 revolution, informal gold mining expanded across the Eastern Desert, with Edfu becoming one of the main departure points for dahaba heading into the mountains. Al-Ray bel-Rash is located near several routes that lead to the Edfu mountains. The proximity of Al-Ray bel-Rash to the desert has pushed some of its residents into informal mining, according to Shazly. The village also became a base for some miners and rock-processing mills, alongside the spread of the drug and arms trades. Stone-crushing and processing mills for quartz extracted from mining sites have spread throughout the area and surrounding villages. “Ever since the mills started operating [in Al-Ray bel-Rash], the electricity has been getting weaker,” Nubi says, as power has been diverted to the small informal processing plants. As gold prospecting brought high-value vehicles, ore and equipment into the area, it also increased the perceived need for armed protection. A mill owner in the village also links the expansion of mining to the spread of weapons, saying that carrying arms has become more common as competition over gold-mining sites intensified around 2018. “I have to get a weapon and ammunition to protect myself,” he explains. The overlap between the two activities is also evident in the most recent campaign itself. According to Bagga, the accusations against Hugairy involve not only stealing villagers’ vehicles, but also vehicles used by the dahaba . Farag attributes the rapid spread of weapons to conflicts erupting in late 2021 over informal mining sites in the Edfu mountains. Groups from tribes in the area were involved, he says, and the repercussions extended to the villages that miners travelled to the mountains from. “After that,” he says, “weapons increased in the village. Everyone wants to protect their crops and livestock.” As possession of rifles became more widespread, a market grew around them. Farag says an automatic rifle costs between LE150,000-200,000, while a bullet costs between LE120-140. Dealers also rent rifles for around LE1,000 a day to anyone who wants one, while ammunition can be bought on credit. If a debtor fails to repay, they could lose their land, car or home. Farag says the deteriorating security situation led him to consider selling his wife’s gold to buy a rifle to protect his family. He also believes that the involvement of members of local families in killings has drawn more people into cycles of pursuit and revenge, lamenting that “the number of thugs in our village increases by one every day.” *** Within this environment, the market for the drug shabu (crystal methamphetamine) has also expanded. Its spread was not limited to Al-Ray bel-Rash. As documented by Mada Masr in June 2025, the entire governorate has seen an expansion in the drug’s circulation, prompting community-led protests and action in several villages and areas across Aswan against drug-selling outlets. Some sources cited in the report linked the rise in shabu use to informal gold mining as it is often used as a stimulant for working long hours in the mountains. Shazly offers another explanation for the difficulty of confronting these activities: the village’s residents belong to multiple families and tribes, unlike some of the valley’s more socially homogeneous villages. In his view, this reduces the residents’ ability to take collective action against the dealers. He says the number of drug users among young people in the village and surrounding communities is constantly increasing. He describes a near-daily phenomenon of users visibly unconscious in the village streets. He also points to a connected increase in theft rate: “They even broke into the village cemetery and stole the iron rods used to build the graves.” In recent years, news outlets have also reported injuries resulting from fights inside the village and deaths as a result of gunshots or hanging , as well as armed clashes connected to the drug trade, some involving dealers and Interior Ministry forces . Among the incidents were clashes that began over competition to open a new drug outlet, the injury of a young man who passed near one of the selling outlets, and other confrontations that lasted for days as a result of disputes between groups linked to the drug trade. But for Shazly, the trade’s impact is more tangible in the reputation that has come to surround the village, increasingly isolating it from its surroundings and other nearby communities. This became particularly clear in 2023, when slogans reading “No to drugs. Shabu means death. Al-Ray bel-Rash is deadly” appeared in central areas of Edfu, as part of a community campaign against drug use. Source: Al-Nabaa Al-Watany newspaper, September 2023 Shazly says some families from surrounding villages have begun refusing their daughters marry young men from the village, “As soon as they find out the groom is from Al-Ray bel-Rash, they tell him, ‘Our daughter won’t live there.’” In June 2025, during protests over the spread of drugs in the governorate, residents of nearby Bassaly blocked the road leading to Al-Ray bel-Rash in protest against the spread of shabu , repeating the same anti-drugs slogans. The valley whose villages were once connected by a shared network of water and agriculture began to see some of its roads closed as fear of its central village grew. Abdou al-Samty, who bought land in Al-Ray bel-Rash about 25 years ago and made a living farming it, recounts how his eldest son began using shabu and then selling drugs. He ultimately kicked his son out. “I’m a simple man with no criminal record. I know nothing but farming. I live in a mud-brick house, and I’m content with earning an honest living,” Samty says. For him, the village that others have come to fear is also the place where he fears for his son, “I don’t want him to grow up, and I don’t want to lose him.” *** The conditions hang heavy over the village. When Mada Masr first visited in 2024, residents pointed to outlets on the main road that they said were used to sell drugs. The same happened during a second visit, in 2025, when the number of outlets appeared to have increased significantly, despite the Interior Ministry having demolished a few. The remains of the demolished structures could be seen in the form of rubble scattered across the farmland surrounding the road. During the first visit, weapons appeared before interviews could begin. As soon as the car transporting the Mada Masr reporter turned into Wadi Radisiyah toward the village, it was followed by a motorcycle carrying two armed men who seemed to have gotten wind of the visit as residents gathered at the host’s home. Upon the reporter entering the house, the two men fired several shots into the air. During the same reporter’s second visit, an armed man stopped them while filming in the village streets, before residents intervened to help them leave. While walking around on both occasions, the reporter saw armed men carrying automatic rifles shopping in village stores, as well as vehicles driving without license plates and fitted with heavy automatic weapons or carrying armed men. Some of the children and teenagers passing by on motorcycles were also carrying weapons. Spent bullet casings were scattered across the ground, and children were collecting and playing with them. A live bullet found by village children in the streets of Al-Ray bel-Rash in northern Aswan, September 2024. Photo: Mada Masr. For Shazly, these scenes shape the rhythm of daily life in the village. As afternoon sets in, activity begins to pick up around the drug outlets, while movement among the rest of the residents declines. Homes shut their doors, women and children venture out less, and travelling outside the village becomes more difficult. “The children kept waking up terrified at night,” Shazly says, as he talks about the gunfire, speculating that a large number of the village’s children deal with unintentional bed-wetting as a result. He has started turning up the television volume at night “so that the children can sleep,” he says, noting that on one occasion, the shooting reached the only primary school in the area during the school hours. Several women across the age spectrum recount similar stories linked to their fears of recurrent violence in the village and how it limits their movement and activities. One of the oldest women in the village, who spoke on condition of anonymity, recalls an entirely different version of life, “We used to go out with our men to plant. The man would work in the land, the woman would make a wicker mat or a dish, and the children would play around them.” Now says she is afraid to even go to her courtyard at night, as bullets often hit the residential properties. She explains that “satellite TV dishes and water tanks across the area are all punctured by bullets.” As for younger women, some say they will often go to the grocery store themselves rather than sending their children, as they fear for their safety amid the speeding cars used by arms and drug dealers and with the village’s streets frequently a scene of car chases and, at times, exchanges of gunfire. They also describe reducing their visits to neighboring villages, where many of their relatives reside, to specific hours of the day. “Now, if a woman stays with friends or family in a neighboring village beyond the afternoon, her husband tells her to stay there,” one of the women says. The women Mada Masr interviewed all share the same worry, in different forms. They are afraid their children will grow up to embody what they are surrounded with: struggling with addiction, entering the circles that deal in weapons and violence, or becoming victims of those circles. For Umm Saber, the fear has already become a reality. When her son objected to a shooting taking place in front of their house in 2024, he was shot dead with three bullets in front of her, she tells Mada Masr. *** Residents who spoke to Mada Masr say security officers sometimes blame them when they call the police for help, accusing them of allowing miners and drug dealers to live among them. Aboul Hassan, a tuk tuk driver from the village, says that in his experience having Al-Ray bel-Rash listed as his address on his national ID card can sometimes be enough to change the way police treat him at checkpoints, resulting in more stops, searches and suspicion. Nevertheless, many residents welcome security campaigns and the deployment of security forces inside the village. When a security force was stationed in Al-Ray bel-Rash following one of the killings, residents said some brought the officers food and tea, while one resident slaughtered a calf to celebrate their presence. The deployment meant people could leave their homes after sunset and sleep without worrying about another round of gunfire. But the force did not remain for long. According to the former police source’s account of one raid, a deployment consisting of three armored vehicles and a large number of cars entered the village before being forced to withdraw after about an hour of heavy gunfire from a small number of armed men. Mada Masr could not independently verify every detail of the incident, but it resembled a pattern that recurred in later reports and played out again on September 5: security deployments enter the village, ensued by clashes in which individuals are killed or injured and weapons are seized, followed by continued operation of illicit activities. Bagga, the village farmer, says the situation has deteriorated further since the beginning of this year. “Every day, you either find a dead person, or someone who has been beaten and robbed on the road, or that a house in the village has been robbed,” he says. “Day and night, the gunfire never stops.” The post How agricultural reclamation village Al-Ray bel-Rash became beset by weapons, drugs and the informal gold trade first appeared on Mada Masr .

items.title: Horoya AC – JS Saoura : « on fera notre mieux pour arracher la qualification », prévient Lotfi Boudraa
items.description: À la veille du match retour du premier tour préliminaire de la Ligue des champions de la CAF, l'entraîneur de la JS Saoura, Lotfi Boudraa, refuse de considérer la victoire 1-0 obtenue à l'aller comme un avantage décisif. Le technicien algérien assure que son équipe abordera cette seconde manche avec le même état d'esprit. « Pour nous, même si on a gagné au match aller, ça reste toujours une mi-temps qu'on a jouée à domicile. On a une deuxième manche, un deuxième match qu'on va jouer. C'est comme si c'était 0-0 en Algérie. On va tout donner ici et que le meilleur gagne ». Conscient de l'atmosphère qui attend ses joueurs au Stade du 28 Septembre, Boudraa s'attend à une rencontre particulièrement disputée face au champion de Guinée, porté par un public heureux de retrouver son équipe dans son enceinte après plusieurs années. « On sait que le Horoya va être soutenu par son public qui n'a pas vu l'équipe jouer 4 ou 5 ans dans ce stade mythique. On sait que ça ne sera pas facile contre cette belle équipe, mais on fera notre mieux pour arracher la qualification ». Battu 1-0 en Algérie, le Horoya AC devra renverser la situation à Conakry pour espérer poursuivre son aventure continentale, tandis que la JS Saoura tentera de préserver son court avantage afin de décrocher son billet pour le tour suivant. Sadjo Bah L’article Horoya AC – JS Saoura : « on fera notre mieux pour arracher la qualification », prévient Lotfi Boudraa est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Ghana undertaking Africa’s largest road infrastructure programme – Agbodza claims
items.description: Roads and Highways Minister Governs Kwame Agbodza claims Ghana is currently undertaking the largest road infrastructure programme in Africa, with major projects being implemented across the country under the government’s Big Push programme. He said the scale of investment in road infrastructure under the programme is unprecedented and represents the government’s response to widespread concerns about the poor condition of roads across the country. Speaking at a citizens’ engagement at the University of Business and Integrated Development Studies in the Upper West Region on Saturday, September 12, Mr Agbodza said poor roads were among the major concerns raised during the 2024 general election campaign. He said President John Dramani Mahama had promised to significantly increase investment in road infrastructure if elected. “When we took office, almost every road in every community was in bad shape. One issue came up very strongly during the 2024 elections, and that is, no one was happy about the road in their neighbourhood, and the president made it a point that when given the opportunity, he would make the kind of investment that we have never seen before,” he said. Mr Agbodza said the government was now translating that commitment into road projects across the country, with all projects under the Big Push programme currently underway. He described the scale of the investment as unprecedented in Ghana and made the broader claim that the country is currently undertaking the largest road infrastructure programme in Africa. “The kind of investment the president is putting into the road infrastructure of our country has never ever been seen in our lifetime. The largest ever road infrastructure project at a particular time in Africa is taking place in Ghana,” he said. “All the Big Push projects are currently in motion, and we have made great progress on all the projects across the country,” he added. The Big Push programme forms part of the government’s infrastructure agenda and involves major road projects across various parts of the country. Mr Agbodza said the government would continue to prioritise road infrastructure in response to the needs of communities and the commitments made during the 2024 election campaign.

items.title: Équipe d’Algérie : pourquoi la FAF doit faire vite pour Mezian Mesloub
items.description: Il n’a pas encore 17 ans mais présente déjà le profil d'un grand joueur d’Europe. Mezian Mesloub, milieu de terrain du RC Lens, attire tous les regards et suscite toutes les convoitises. Pour sa carrière internationale, il peut jouer pour le Portugal, l’Algérie ou la France. Jeudi, il a éclaboussé de son talent la plus prestigieuse compétition interclubs au monde, la Ligue des Champions d’Europe. Fils de l’ex-international algérien Walid Mesloub, le jeune talent est convoqué depuis 2025 chez les jeunes catégories du Portugal, où il a des origines par sa mère. La France, où il est né, voudra sans doute s’attacher ses services s'il continue sur cette lancée. La bataille pourrait être rude dans quelques années. Mezian Mesloub se distingue en Ligue des Champions Mezian Mesloub a disputé son premier match professionnel avec le RC Lens en mai dernier, à l’occasion de la 33e journée de Ligue 1 contre Nantes. Il a marqué quelques secondes après son entrée en cours de jeu, permettant à son club de gagner (1-0) et de valider sa place en ligue des champions. En fin de saison, il est devenu, à 16 ans, vice-champion de France. A l’intersaison, il était convoité par le Benfica et le PSV Eindhoven, mais il a préféré signer un contrat professionnel avec son club formateur. Jeudi 10 septembre, il a disputé son premier match de Ligue des Champions à 16 ans et 306 jours. Entré en deuxième mi-temps sur le terrain du Slavia Prague, il a mis tout le monde d'accord, livrant une grosse prestation ponctuée par une passe décisive sur l’égalisation de son équipe (2-2) en fin de match. La rencontre a été remportée par les Lençois 3-2. “Je crois très fort en lui”, a avoué son entraîneur, l’Allemand Dino Toppmöller. Algérie – France- Portugal : pour qui optera Mezian Mesloub ? La liste des prétendants devrait s’allonger au fil de la saison. Mais la véritable bataille qui s'annonce est celle que livreront peut-être dans quelques années les trois sélections pour lesquelles le joueur est éligible. Mezian Mesloub est né en 2010 à Martigues (France) d’un père algérien et d’une mère ayant des origines portugaises. Les Portugais ont pris une longueur d’avance en le convoquant dès 2025 chez les U16 (3 matchs, un but) puis les U17 avec lesquels il a disputé cinq rencontres et marqué une fois. Mais le choix n'est pas définitif. Le parcours de son père, qui a disputé sept matchs avec les Verts entre 2010 et 2016, pourrait peser en faveur de l’Algérie. De même que le joueur pourrait être tenté par l’équipe de France, l’une des meilleures au monde, si l’occasion lui est donnée. En tout cas, la fédération algérienne de football doit faire vite et ne pas attendre que le joueur atteigne un niveau qui lui ouvrirait les portes des Bleus ou de la sélection du Portugal. Du reste, la nouvelle stratégie de l’Algérie avec les jeunes talents nés en Europe est de les “sécuriser” avant qu'ils n'atteignent la catégorie seniors. L’article Équipe d’Algérie : pourquoi la FAF doit faire vite pour Mezian Mesloub est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Tinubu edges Obi by 1,067 responses in Oxford-Metro poll
items.description: President Bola Tinubu finished ahead of Peter Obi by 1,067 responses in the Oxford–Metro Analytics’ National Trust Poll. The ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‌‍⁠‌‌⁠‍​​‌​poll, which closed on Sept. 7, recorded a total of 69,110 approved and unflagged responses in its final analytical dataset. Tinubu received 24,469 responses, representing 35.41 per cent of the total responses, while Obi polled 23,402, representing 33.86 per cent of the total responses. Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar came third with 18,430 responses, representing 26.67 per cent of the total participation. The result gave Tinubu an advantage of 1,067 responses over Obi, translating to approximately 1.54 percentage points. The poll’s regional distribution, however, suggested a significantly different electoral map from the outcome of the 2023 presidential election. Tinubu, who won 12 states in the 2023 presidential election, was reported to have led in 20 states and the Federal Capital Territory in the online poll. Meanwhile, Obi and Atiku recorded the highest number of responses each in eight states. The strongest changes were recorded in parts of Northern Nigeria , where the poll indicated growing support for Tinubu. Tinubu led in Kaduna, Katsina and Gombe, which were states won by Atiku during the 2023 presidential election. He also led in Kano, where New Nigeria Peoples Party (NNPP) candidate, Rabiu Kwankwaso won the presidential vote in 2023. At the regional level, Tinubu led in the South-West, North-West and North-Central geopolitical zones. Obi recorded his strongest performances in the South-East and South-South, while Atiku led the North-East. In the South-West, Tinubu received 10,968 responses, representing 43.53 per cent of the region’s total participation. He also led in the North-West with 4,129 responses, accounting for 43.10 per cent of responses from the zone. In the North-Central, Tinubu secured 6,370 responses, representing 36.97 per cent of the regional total. Obi’s strongest regional performance came from the South-East, where he received 5,796 responses, representing 63.97 per cent. The Labour Party candidate also led the South-South with 2,389 responses, accounting for 41.48 per cent of participants in the region. Atiku dominated the North-East, where he received 1,235 responses, representing 55.46 per cent of the region’s total. In spite of Tinubu’s wider geographical spread, the national contest remained remarkably close between the leading candidates. The difference of 1,067 responses between Tinubu and Obi underscored the narrow margin separating the two leading contenders. Some individual state contests were considerably closer than the broader regional figures suggested. In Kogi, for instance, Tinubu received 39 responses, Atiku 38 and Obi 33 out of only 110 responses recorded. The one-response difference between Tinubu and Atiku in Kogi demonstrated the importance of considering the relatively small participation base in interpreting the figures. In the FCT, Tinubu secured 5,599 responses against Obi’s 5,278, giving him a lead of 321 responses, while Atiku received 3,954. In Rivers, Tinubu polled 975 responses, compared with Obi’s 892 and Atiku’s 568, leaving an 83-response margin between the two leading candidates. Beyond the three leading candidates, Omoyele Sowore received 1,016 responses, followed by Seyi Makinde with 519 and former President Goodluck Jonathan with 284. Anita Zugwai-Chukwu received 18 responses, Sandy Onor received six responses, while Prince Kennedy Ahanotu recorded two responses. Another 638 participants selected the option, “I Do Not Trust Any Candidate Yet,” while 204 respondents were undecided and 122 selected “Other Candidate.” The distribution showed that winning the overall tally did not necessarily translate into dominating every geopolitical zone or state. Tinubu’s lead nationally and across three geopolitical zones contrasted with Obi’s dominance in the South-East and Atiku’s strength in the North-East. However, participation was heavily concentrated geographically, with Lagos and the FCT alone accounting for 54.44 per cent of all responses. The final dataset also contained 56 diaspora responses, which were excluded from the six domestic regional tallies. (NAN) The post Tinubu edges Obi by 1,067 responses in Oxford-Metro poll appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: INEC final list confirms Yahaya Bello as APC candidate for Kogi Central
items.description: By Omeiza Ajayi The Independent National Electoral Commission INEC has released its final list of candidates for the Kogi Central, Kogi East and Kogi West senatorial districts ahead of the January 2027 presidential and National Assembly elections, confirming former Governor Yahaya Bello as the candidate of the All Progressives Congress APC for the Kogi Central seat. The list, containing a total of 42 candidates across the three senatorial districts, was signed by the Secretary of INEC, Rose Oriaran-Anthony, and captures the names, parties, ages, gender and qualifications of all cleared aspirants. Bello, 51, is listed alongside ten other contenders for the Kogi Central seat, including Suzan Jagbadi of the Accord (A), Muhammad Jatto of the African Action Congress (AA), Babalawale Habib of the Action Peoples Party (APP), Ogembe Salau Ahmed of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Muhammed Aminu of the All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA), Suleiman Isah of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), Salau Muritala Audu of the National Democratic Coalition (NDC), Onuja Umar Sunday of the Peoples Redemption Party (PRP) and Bashir Yusuf of the Social Democratic Party (SDP). Also on the Kogi Central list is the incumbent senator, Natasha Akpoti-Uduaghan, who is seeking re-election on the platform of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP). The list describes her qualifications as a First School Leaving Certificate, Senior School Certificate Examination and a Bachelor of Laws (LL.B). Bello’s emergence as the APC standard-bearer followed a turbulent build-up marked by uncertainty over his eligibility. A pressure group, the Kogi APC Renaissance Forum, had warned months earlier that imposing the former governor on the party would cost it the senatorial seat, citing what it called his weak grassroots acceptance even within his home constituency. Speculation also trailed his screening process, with reports suggesting complications that could have kept him out of the race entirely, before the party’s screening committee eventually cleared him alongside other aspirants from the three senatorial districts. Bello reportedly went on to win the APC primary for Kogi Central by a wide margin, polling 72,399 votes across the five local government areas of the district against 319 votes for his closest rival, Ibrahim Yakubu Adoke, and 188 votes for another aspirant, Momoh Yusuf Obaro. For Kogi East, the list includes 17 candidates contesting under various parties, among them Ameh Erico Joseph of the APC, Ochija Berikisu of the Democracy for the Liberation of Africa (DLA), Ojogbane Paul Ilemona of the National Democratic Party (NDP) and Muhammed Abdullahi of the PDP. In Kogi West, 14 candidates are in contention, led by Karimi Sunday of the APC, Musa Ibrahim Ahmadu of the ADC and Yusuf Ayo Tajudeen of the PDP. The document lists no candidate as living with disability across all three districts, with the “PWD” column uniformly marked “None,” while ages of the candidates range from 36 to 73 years. items.title: Prospective homeowners troop to Day 2 of JoyNews-Republic Bank Habitat Fair, engage experts on homeownership
items.description: Prospective homeowners have trooped to Day two of the JoyNews–Republic Bank Habitat Fair at the Marina Mall in Accra, taking advantage of the event to seek answers to questions surrounding homeownership. The second day of the three-day fair, which runs from Friday, September 11 to Sunday, September 13, has attracted individuals and families looking to buy, build, renovate or improve their homes. Visitors have been engaging exhibitors and industry professionals, asking questions about mortgage financing, property acquisition, construction, home improvement and other areas of the housing sector. For many prospective homeowners, financing remains a major consideration, with Republic Bank Ghana offering visitors the opportunity to engage its representatives and learn more about mortgage options, eligibility requirements and repayment plans. The bank’s mortgage solutions are available to salaried workers, self-employed professionals, entrepreneurs and business owners seeking to purchase, build or renovate their homes. Beyond financing, patrons at the fair are also exploring products and services from businesses operating across the housing and property sector. Exhibitors are showcasing solutions covering real estate, construction, interior décor, security, renewable energy, technology and mobility. The interactions have provided prospective homeowners with an opportunity to compare options, seek professional advice and gain practical information to guide their homeownership decisions. The fair brings together leading businesses and professionals in Ghana’s housing and property sector under one roof, providing visitors with direct access to experts across different stages of the homeownership journey. The JoyNews–Republic Bank Habitat Fair continues at the Marina Mall throughout Saturday, September 12, before ending on Sunday, September 13. – Photo Credit: David Andoh

items.title: Iraq closes three border crossings with Iran after drone launch
items.description: Iraq closed three border crossings with Iran on Saturday, officials told AFP, after a drone attack on a Saudi Arabian pipeline that both Riyadh and Baghdad said was launched from Iraq. Following the Friday night attack, Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi dismissed the military commander in Missan province, on the Iran border, after authorities determined that the drones had been launched from there. Two Iraqi security sources told AFP on Saturday that drone launchers were found near a border crossing in Missan. No group has claimed responsibility for the attack, and an alliance of powerful Tehran-backed Iraqi armed groups said they hadn’t struck the pipeline, though Riyadh has previously accused the groups of targeting its oil infrastructure. An Iraqi security source and a government official told AFP that authorities ordered the closing of three border crossings with Iran. The security source said the decision was “part of an intelligence effort to track down the perpetrators and prevent their escape… and to hinder the smuggling of drones through these crossings”. Both sources, who spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not allowed to speak to the media, could not specify when the crossings would reopen. The closed crossings are Shalamsheh in Basra province, al-Shib in Missan and al-Mandali in the central province of Diyala. Other border crossings with Iran are still open. A security official said that “security forces found drone launchers near the Iraq-Iran border in the al-Tib” region, a remote part of Missan, close to the al-Shib crossing. A second security source gave the same account. Zaidi’s military spokesperson Sabah al-Numan said the prime minister had approved “Iran’s request to conduct a joint investigation into finding drone launch platforms near the Iraq-Iran border”. The government’s security media cell said earlier that authorities “have started administrative and security reorganisation operations at several border crossings”. It added that they had stepped up “intelligence activities” to determine “the breaches and violations that took place at these crossings”. It later announced that passengers stranded for hours at two crossings were permitted to pass. In July, the United States and Saudi Arabia said they had struck Iran-backed militants in Iraq in response to attacks on US forces and Saudi oil facilities. Pro-Iran armed groups have supported Tehran during the Middle East war, claiming hundreds of attacks on US bases in Iraq and across the region. On Saturday, those groups, operating under the umbrella of the Islamic Resistance in Iraq, said they had not struck the pipeline. It is “an honour that we do not claim”, the Islamic Resistance said in a statement. Under mounting US pressure, Zaidi has pledged to ensure that armed factions surrender their weapons to the state. The issue has fuelled tensions in recent weeks, with several groups refusing to disarm. AFP The post Iraq closes three border crossings with Iran after drone launch appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: France sink Germany to reach first women’s basketball World Cup final
items.description: France are through to the final of the women’s basketball World Cup for the first time after a 86-64 victory over host nation Germany on Saturday. Gabby Williams top scored with 22 points for the Olympic silver medalists, who kept their unbeaten record at the tournament alive before Sunday’s decider in Berlin. The US-born Williams, who also topped the assist charts with five and with four had the most steals, was the constant threat on both ends of the floor for the French. France are on track to face the United States and will hope to avenge their one-point defeat in the Olympic final in Paris in 2024, should the heavily favoured Americans get past Spain later on Saturday. The 11-time champion United States are on a 34-game winning streak at the World Cup dating back to their surprise semi-final defeat at the hands of Russia in 2006. The underdog Germans swept past European champions Belgium in their quarter-final clash for a first semi-final appearance as a unified country, with East Germany having made the final four in 1967. France burst out of the blocks early but the Germans stayed hot on their heels, trailing by just two at quarter-time. France’s quality told as the match went on and the French scored nine straight points to start the second-half, running out to a 16-point lead. Alexis Peterson and Emily Bessoir hit threes in the final quarter as the Germans cut the lead to just eight to stay within striking distance, but France again went on a run, scoring 12 straight to end the match and seal progress to a maiden final. items.title: Islamabad IG Ali Nasir Rizvi transferred, appointed NCCIA director general
items.description: The federal government on Saturday transferred BS-20 officer Syed Ali Nasir Rizvi from his post as inspector general of Islamabad Capital Territory (ICT) Police and appointed him director general of the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA), according to a notification issued by the Establishment Division. The notification said the transfer and appointment had been made with the approval of the federal government under Section 29(3) of the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act, 2016, as amended by the Prevention of Electronic Crimes (Amendment) Act, 2025, and Section 10 of the Civil Servants Act, 1973. The order takes “immediate effect and until further orders”. Under Section 29(3), the government can appoint the NCCIA chief for a non-extendable term of three years. Meanwhile, the outgoing Rizvi’s post will be filled by Captain (retd) Muhammad Sohail Chaudhry, who is currently serving “under the Government of Punjab”, according to a separate notification. Syed Ali Nasir Rizvi was appointed Islamabad IG on March 29, 2024, after having served in Punjab.

items.title: Police interdict officer over death of 23-year-old law student, Ivan Baidoo
items.description: The Ghana Police Service has interdicted General Corporal Robert Koranteng in connection with the death of 23-year-old law student of Central University, Ivan Baidoo. The interdiction follows initial investigations into a viral video concerning the incident, which occurred on the Tema Motorway on August 27, 2026. The Police Service, in a statement issued on Saturday, September 12, said the Homicide Unit of the Criminal Investigations Department (CID) is intensifying efforts to establish the full circumstances surrounding Mr Baidoo’s death. It said that the Police Professional Standards Bureau (PPSB) has also been tasked with investigating the conduct of General Corporal Koranteng in connection with the incident. items.title: Bachir Belloumi inscrit un magnifique doublé face à Chelsea en Premier League
items.description: Bachir Belloumi frappe fort en Premier League. L’attaquant international algérien de Hull City a inscrit son premier et magnifique doublé dans le championnat anglais face à Chelsea (2-2) ce samedi 12 septembre lors de la 4 e journée du championnat d’Angleterre. Le fils de la légende du football algérien Lakhdar Belloumi a d’abord égalisé à la 28 e minute d’une reprise de volée imparable, avant de donner l’avantage à son équipe six minutes après (2-1, 34 e ) en reprenant aussi un centre pour battre le gardien adverse. Mais son équipe n’a pas pu conserver son avantage face aux hommes de l’Espagnol Xabi Alonso. Chelsea est revenue au score à la 66 e minute par Pedro (2-2), soit six minutes après la sortie de l’attaquant algérien. Mohamed Belloumi a marqué 2 buts face à Chelsea. pic.twitter.com/0iuV2VuunL — 𝗠𝗘𝗥𝗖𝗨. (@CompsMercu) September 12, 2026 Premier League : Bachir Belloumi ouvre son compteur buts avec un doublé Pour son retour en Premier League, Hull City rate l’occasion de s’imposer sur la pelouse d’une équipe qui fait partie du big six. Malgré ce match nul, l’équipe de l’international algérien garde la 3 e place au classement avec 8 points, à un point du duo Man City – Arsenal qui occupent ex-aequo la première place avec 9 points chacun. Avec ce doublé, Bachir Belloumi, 24 ans, consolide sa place de buteur de Hull City en Premier League. Son équipe a remporté deux victoires contre Manchester United (2-0) et Coventry (1-0) et fait match nul deux fois face à Aston Villa (0-0) et Chelsea (2-2).
